name: Peter T. Paul College of Business and Economics
use: Business school: classrooms, group study rooms, Great Hall, cafe
style: Contemporary collegiate: brick and slate-roofed wings around a courtyard, glass-and-fin Great Hall

facts.text: Designed by Goody Clancy and built by PC Construction; ground broken May 3, 2011 and dedicated April 12, 2013.
Named for Peter T. Paul (class of 1967), whose $25 million gift in 2008 founded the new business school.
The school was formerly the Whittemore School of Business and Economics, housed in McConnell Hall until the move in 2013.
About 115,000 sq ft, four stories, LEED Gold certified, with 950 instructional seats in 16 classrooms, 25 group study rooms, a cafe, a commercial kitchen and a two-story Great Hall.
A Goody Clancy lead designer (later principal) shared design leadership of the project.

verdict: The campus's best modern building: brick-and-slate wings around a landscaped courtyard and a finned glass Great Hall that students call the best place to study.
notes: Photos (2013, months after opening) show a brick-and-slate courtyard building with a double-height glass Great Hall wrapped in vertical fins; strong daylight into the Great Hall, high ceilings there. No interior licensed photo found. Old row said 2011 as year; opening/dedication is 2013, so built=2013. Old claims of an AIANH Honor Award 2014, ~45% below ASHRAE baseline, a 40-ft kinetic sculpture and a ~$50M cost were not confirmed from pages I could open (world-architects.com and aianh.org blocked or 404); sq ft varies by source (110k–120k). Gorelco page is a contractor portfolio. Air conditioning not documented on an opened page.
judgeNotes: Photos confirm a confident courtyard composition. Character 7 rather than 8: distinctive, but only 13 years of story.
